=== Speicherstadt Queues (Even Rotation) ===

There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Each player is privately dealt a different contract colour, drawn at random from the 6 without repetition. No one else learns it. Each player starts with 6 coins and no goods. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).
6. RESOLVE Lot 1, then Lot 2, then Lot 3: The queue for a lot is every player with a positive number on it, ordered by this round's priority order. Let k be the queue length. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by 1, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price 1. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. A lot with an empty queue is discarded. Coins spent on an earlier lot this round count when checking later lots.
7. ANNOUNCE: For each lot, announce which players queued, who bought it (if anyone) and the price paid. Limits are never revealed. Every player's coins and goods held (with colours) are public at all times.
8. END CHECK: After round 12 the deck is empty and the game ends.

FINAL SCORING: Each player's score is their coins, plus 5 points for each good of their own contract colour, plus 2 points for each good of any other colour. All contract colours are then revealed.

The player with the highest final score wins. If several tie for highest, the tied player with more goods of their own contract colour wins. If they are still tied, they share the win as a draw.

There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Each player is privately dealt a different contract colour, drawn at random from the 6 without repetition. No one else learns it. Each player starts with 6 coins and no goods. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).
6. RESOLVE Lot 1, then Lot 2, then Lot 3: The queue for a lot is every player with a positive number on it, ordered by this round's priority order. Let k be the queue length. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by 1, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price 1. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. A lot with an empty queue is discarded. Coins spent on an earlier lot this round count when checking later lots.

1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.

4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. === Speicherstadt Queues (Even Rotation) ===

There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Each player is privately dealt a different contract colour, drawn at random from the 6 without repetition. No one else learns it. Each player starts with 6 coins and no goods. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).
6. RESOLVE Lot 1, then Lot 2, then Lot 3: The queue for a lot is every player with a positive number on it, ordered by this round's priority order. Let k be the queue length. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by 1, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price 1. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. A lot with an empty queue is discarded. Coins spent on an earlier lot this round count when checking later lots.
7. ANNOUNCE: For each lot, announce which players queued, who bought it (if anyone) and the price paid. Limits are never revealed. Every player's coins and goods held (with colours) are public at all times.
8. END CHECK: After round 12 the deck is empty and the game ends.

FINAL SCORING: Each player's score is their coins, plus 5 points for each good of their own contract colour, plus 2 points for each good of any other colour. All contract colours are then revealed.

Think about the rules, the other players and what they have done, then act. When you are asked to act, reply with exactly one legal answer in the form the question asks for, and keep any reasoning short and before the answer. Do not ask questions back.

=== Speicherstadt Queues (Even Rotation) ===

There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Each player is privately dealt a different contract colour, drawn at random from the 6 without repetition. No one else learns it. Each player starts with 6 coins and no goods. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).
6. RESOLVE Lot 1, then Lot 2, then Lot 3: The queue for a lot is every player with a positive number on it, ordered by this round's priority order. Let k be the queue length. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by 1, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price 1. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. A lot with an empty queue is discarded. Coins spent on an earlier lot this round count when checking later lots.
7. ANNOUNCE: For each lot, announce which players queued, who bought it (if anyone) and the price paid. Limits are never revealed. Every player's coins and goods held (with colours) are public at all times.
8. END CHECK: After round 12 the deck is empty and the game ends.

FINAL SCORING: Each player's score is their coins, plus 5 points for each good of their own contract colour, plus 2 points for each good of any other colour. All contract colours are then revealed.

The player with the highest final score wins. If several tie for highest, the tied player with more goods of their own contract colour wins. If they are still tied, they share the win as a draw.

Each player is privately dealt a different contract colour, drawn at random from the 6 without repetition. No one else learns it. Each player starts with 6 coins and no goods. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).
6. RESOLVE Lot 1, then Lot 2, then Lot 3: The queue for a lot is every player with a positive number on it, ordered by this round's priority order. Let k be the queue length. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by 1, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price 1. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. A lot with an empty queue is discarded. Coins spent on an earlier lot this round count when checking later lots.
7. ANNOUNCE: For each lot, announce which players queued, who bought it (if anyone) and the price paid. Limits are never revealed. Every player's coins and goods held (with colours) are public at all times.
8. END CHECK: After round 12 the deck is empty and the game ends.

FINAL SCORING: Each player's score is their coins, plus 5 points for each good of their own contract colour, plus 2 points for each good of any other colour. All contract colours are then revealed.

The player with the highest final score wins. If several tie for highest, the tied player with more goods of their own contract colour wins. If they are still tied, they share the win as a draw.

There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).

The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by 1, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price 1. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. 1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.

4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).

There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).

=== Speicherstadt Queues (Even Rotation) ===

There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Each player is privately dealt a different contract colour, drawn at random from the 6 without repetition. No one else learns it. Each player starts with 6 coins and no goods. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).
6. RESOLVE Lot 1, then Lot 2, then Lot 3: The queue for a lot is every player with a positive number on it, ordered by this round's priority order. Let k be the queue length. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by 1, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price 1. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. A lot with an empty queue is discarded. Coins spent on an earlier lot this round count when checking later lots.
7. ANNOUNCE: For each lot, announce which players queued, who bought it (if anyone) and the price paid. Limits are never revealed. Every player's coins and goods held (with colours) are public at all times.
8. END CHECK: After round 12 the deck is empty and the game ends.

FINAL SCORING: Each player's score is their coins, plus 5 points for each good of their own contract colour, plus 2 points for each good of any other colour. All contract colours are then revealed.

Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).
6. RESOLVE Lot 1, then Lot 2, then Lot 3: The queue for a lot is every player with a positive number on it, ordered by this round's priority order. Let k be the queue length. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by 1, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price 1. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. === Speicherstadt Queues (Even Rotation) ===

There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Each player is privately dealt a different contract colour, drawn at random from the 6 without repetition. No one else learns it. Each player starts with 6 coins and no goods. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).
6. RESOLVE Lot 1, then Lot 2, then Lot 3: The queue for a lot is every player with a positive number on it, ordered by this round's priority order. Let k be the queue length. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).

If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. 5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. 1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).

Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.

records.system: You are one player in a game on the XColos platform, played by turns. You know only what the game tells you; other players' hidden information is hidden from you as yours is from them. Your goal is to win. Think about the rules, the other players and what they have done, then act. When you are asked to act, reply with exactly one legal answer in the form the question asks for, and keep any reasoning short and before the answer. Do not ask questions back.

[user]
=== Speicherstadt Queues (Even Rotation) ===

There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Each player is privately dealt a different contract colour, drawn at random from the 6 without repetition. No one else learns it. Each player starts with 6 coins and no goods. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).
6. RESOLVE Lot 1, then Lot 2, then Lot 3: The queue for a lot is every player with a positive number on it, ordered by this round's priority order. Let k be the queue length. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by 1, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price 1. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. A lot with an empty queue is discarded. Coins spent on an earlier lot this round count when checking later lots.
7. ANNOUNCE: For each lot, announce which players queued, who bought it (if anyone) and the price paid. Limits are never revealed. Every player's coins and goods held (with colours) are public at all times.
8. END CHECK: After round 12 the deck is empty and the game ends.

FINAL SCORING: Each player's score is their coins, plus 5 points for each good of their own contract colour, plus 2 points for each good of any other colour. All contract colours are then revealed.

The player with the highest final score wins. If several tie for highest, the tied player with more goods of their own contract colour wins. If they are still tied, they share the win as a draw.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seats are numbered from 1 upwards in seating order. Priority rotates through the seats in this order.
The deck of 36 cards (6 of each of 6 colours) is shuffled.
Each player has been dealt a secret contract colour.
You start with: You are seat 1. coins 6, contract Orange, goods [], limit1 0, limit2 0, limit3 0, own_goods 0, score 0. you know seat 2 coins 6, goods [], score 0; seat 3 coins 6, goods [], score 0; seat 4 coins 6, goods [], score 0. buyer1 0, buyer2 0, buyer3 0, cards_per_colour 6, coin_points 1, colours 6, contract_good_points 5, deck_size 36, discard [], income_per_round 2, limit_max 6, limit_min 0, lot1 , lot2 , lot3 , lot_sold False, lots_per_round 3, lowest_offer_price 1, offer_price 0, other_good_points 2, price1 0, price2 0, price3 0, price_drop_per_decline 1, priority_order [], priority_start 1, q1 [], q2 [], q3 [], queue_len 0, round 0, rounds 12, starting_coins 6, tiebreak_multiplier 100, workers_per_player 2. still playing: 1, 2, 3, 4.

Each round runs in this order: supply → income → priority → talk → limit on lot 1 → limit on lot 2 → limit on lot 3 → worker cap → lot 1 setup → lot 1 offers → lot 1 discard → lot 2 setup → lot 2 offers → lot 2 discard → lot 3 setup → lot 3 offers → lot 3 discard → round report → final scoring → after the last round.

Actions you may be asked for:
  talk         answer with what you want to say
  limit_on_lot_1 answer with a whole number, in the range you are given
  limit_on_lot_2 answer with a whole number, in the range you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

Each player is privately dealt a different contract colour, drawn at random from the 6 without repetition. No one else learns it. Each player starts with 6 coins and no goods. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).
6. RESOLVE Lot 1, then Lot 2, then Lot 3: The queue for a lot is every player with a positive number on it, ordered by this round's priority order. Let k be the queue length. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by 1, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price 1. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. A lot with an empty queue is discarded. Coins spent on an earlier lot this round count when checking later lots.
7. ANNOUNCE: For each lot, announce which players queued, who bought it (if anyone) and the price paid. Limits are never revealed. Every player's coins and goods held (with colours) are public at all times.
8. END CHECK: After round 12 the deck is empty and the game ends.

FINAL SCORING: Each player's score is their coins, plus 5 points for each good of their own contract colour, plus 2 points for each good of any other colour. All contract colours are then revealed.

The player with the highest final score wins. If several tie for highest, the tied player with more goods of their own contract colour wins. If they are still tied, they share the win as a draw.

There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).

If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by 1, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price 1. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. === Speicherstadt Queues (Even Rotation) ===

There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Each player is privately dealt a different contract colour, drawn at random from the 6 without repetition. No one else learns it. Each player starts with 6 coins and no goods. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).
6. RESOLVE Lot 1, then Lot 2, then Lot 3: The queue for a lot is every player with a positive number on it, ordered by this round's priority order. Let k be the queue length. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by 1, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price 1. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. A lot with an empty queue is discarded. Coins spent on an earlier lot this round count when checking later lots.
7. ANNOUNCE: For each lot, announce which players queued, who bought it (if anyone) and the price paid. Limits are never revealed. Every player's coins and goods held (with colours) are public at all times.
8. END CHECK: After round 12 the deck is empty and the game ends.

FINAL SCORING: Each player's score is their coins, plus 5 points for each good of their own contract colour, plus 2 points for each good of any other colour. All contract colours are then revealed.

The player with the highest final score wins. If several tie for highest, the tied player with more goods of their own contract colour wins. If they are still tied, they share the win as a draw.

1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).

There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Each player is privately dealt a different contract colour, drawn at random from the 6 without repetition. No one else learns it. Each player starts with 6 coins and no goods. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).
6. RESOLVE Lot 1, then Lot 2, then Lot 3: The queue for a lot is every player with a positive number on it, ordered by this round's priority order. Let k be the queue length. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by 1, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price 1. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. A lot with an empty queue is discarded. Coins spent on an earlier lot this round count when checking later lots.
7. ANNOUNCE: For each lot, announce which players queued, who bought it (if anyone) and the price paid. Limits are never revealed. Every player's coins and goods held (with colours) are public at all times.
8. END CHECK: After round 12 the deck is empty and the game ends.

=== Speicherstadt Queues (Even Rotation) ===

There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Each player is privately dealt a different contract colour, drawn at random from the 6 without repetition. No one else learns it. Each player starts with 6 coins and no goods. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).

1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).

If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
There are 6 colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has 36 cards, 6 of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Each player is privately dealt a different contract colour, drawn at random from the 6 without repetition. No one else learns it. Each player starts with 6 coins and no goods. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly 12 rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains 2 coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from 0 to 6. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has 2 workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).
6. RESOLVE Lot 1, then Lot 2, then Lot 3: The queue for a lot is every player with a positive number on it, ordered by this round's priority order. Let k be the queue length. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by 1, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price 1. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. A lot with an empty queue is discarded. Coins spent on an earlier lot this round count when checking later lots.
7. ANNOUNCE: For each lot, announce which players queued, who bought it (if anyone) and the price paid. Limits are never revealed. Every player's coins and goods held (with colours) are public at all times.
8. END CHECK: After round 12 the deck is empty and the game ends.

FINAL SCORING: Each player's score is their coins, plus 5 points for each good of their own contract colour, plus 2 points for each good of any other colour. All contract colours are then revealed.

The player with the highest final score wins. If several tie for highest, the tied player with more goods of their own contract colour wins. If they are still tied, they share the win as a draw.
